known_facts_book1: One of four little Rabbits — with Flopsy, Mopsy and Cotton-tail — who live with their mother in a sand-bank under a big fir-tree.
Described as 'very naughty', unlike his sisters, who go blackberrying instead.
Runs straight to Mr. McGregor's garden and squeezes under the gate while his sisters go down the lane.
Eats lettuces, French beans and radishes, then goes looking for parsley, feeling rather sick.
Is spotted by Mr. McGregor near a cucumber frame; McGregor jumps up and chases him, waving a rake and shouting 'Stop thief!'
Loses one shoe among the cabbages and the other among the potatoes during the chase.
Runs into a gooseberry net and is caught by the brass buttons of his new blue jacket; wriggles free, leaving the jacket behind.
Is overheard crying by some friendly sparrows, who fly to him and implore him to exert himself.
Hides from a sieve McGregor tries to pop over him by jumping into a can inside the tool-shed.
Gives himself away by sneezing 'Kertyschoo!' while hiding under a flower-pot search.
Jumps out of a window to escape, upsetting three plants; the window is too small for McGregor to follow.
Asks an old mouse the way to the gate, but she cannot answer because her mouth is full of a pea.
Sees a white cat staring at goldfish by a pond and avoids speaking to her, remembering what his cousin Benjamin Bunny told him about cats.
Climbs onto a wheelbarrow and spots the gate while Mr. McGregor is hoeing onions with his back turned.
Slips under the gate to safety in the wood, leaving his jacket and shoes behind in the garden.
It is the second jacket and pair of shoes he has lost in a fortnight.
Runs home without stopping to the big fir-tree and collapses on the sand floor of the rabbit-hole, exhausted.
Is unwell that evening; his mother puts him to bed and doses him with camomile tea instead of supper.
His sisters Flopsy, Mopsy and Cotton-tail have bread, milk and blackberries for supper instead of camomile tea.

known_relations_book1.Mrs. Rabbit: His mother; warns him against the garden before he goes, and puts him to bed with camomile tea after his ordeal.
known_relations_book1.Mr. McGregor: Chases him through the garden with a rake and later a sieve; the direct antagonist of the chase. Never catches him.
known_relations_book1.Flopsy: One of his three sisters, who behaves well and goes blackberrying instead of raiding the garden.
